items.title: The Hamilton-Jacobi equation of a declared potential presentation: the class of action-dimension functions $S$ with $S_t+H(t,q,S_q)=0$ in one momentum chart
items.statement:
Adopt the force model with potential presentation $(U,d)$ and mechanical
Lagrangian $L=K-U$ of [[def-cm07-action-and-mechanical-lagrangian]] with the
data and conventions of [[def-cm12-cotangent-momentum]]: masses
$m_{1},\dots,m_{N}>0$, open configuration domain $Q\subseteq\mathbb R^{3N}$,
time window $I_{0}$, mass operator $\mathsf M$
([[def-cm01-configuration]]), $C^{2}$ potential $U$ and residual forces $d$
of the standing regularity ([[def-cm03-potential-and-mechanical-energy]],
[[post-cm02-force-superposition]]). Assume the presentation is hyperregular
on its charts, with the Hamiltonians $H$ and $\widetilde H$ and inverse
Legendre branches of [[def-cm12-hamiltonian]],
[[def-cm12-hyperregularity]],
[[pthm-cm12-mechanical-hyperregularity]]. The momentum charts, their forms
and their canonical coordinates are those of [[def-cm13-two-form]] and
[[def-cm13-canonical-form]]; dimensions are read by [[def-cm01-units]] and
differentiability classes are those of
[[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]].

**(a) The chart datum.** Fix one momentum chart of the presentation: either
the Cartesian chart with the coordinates $(t,x,p)$ on
$I_{0}\times Q\times\mathbb R^{3N}$ and the Hamiltonian $H$ of
[[def-cm12-hamiltonian]] clause (a), or the chart of a
generalized-coordinate map $X:\Omega\to Q$ with $r$ coordinates, the
coordinates $(t,q,p)$ on $I_{0}\times\Omega\times\mathbb R^{r}$ and the
Hamiltonian $\widetilde H$ of clause (b). Write $m\in\{3N,r\}$ for the
number of momentum pairs, let $V\subseteq\mathbb R^{m}$ denote the
configuration-coordinate domain of the chart ($Q$ in the Cartesian case,
$\Omega$ in the other), and write $H$ for the corresponding Hamiltonian,

$$H:I_{0}\times V\times\mathbb R^{m}\longrightarrow\mathbb R,\qquad (t,q,p)\longmapsto H(t,q,p),$$

a function of class $C^{2}$ and dimension $\mu\ell^{2}\tau^{-2}$ (energy) by
[[pthm-cm12-mechanical-hyperregularity]]. Let $J'\subseteq I_{0}$,
$U'\subseteq V$ and $A'\subseteq\mathbb R^{m}$ be nonempty open sets
([[def-metric-topology]], [[def-interval]]).

**(b) Solutions of the equation.** A map

$$S:J'\times U'\times A'\longrightarrow\mathbb R,\qquad (t,q,\alpha)\longmapsto S(t,q,\alpha),$$

of class $C^{3}$ **solves the Hamilton-Jacobi equation associated with $H$
on $J'\times U'\times A'$** when

$$S_{t}(t,q,\alpha)+H\bigl(t,\,q,\,S_{q}(t,q,\alpha)\bigr)=0\qquad\bigl((t,q,\alpha)\in J'\times U'\times A'\bigr),$$
where $S_{t}$ is the partial derivative in $t$ and
$S_{q}=(S_{q^{1}},\dots,S_{q^{m}})$ is the gradient in $q$
([[def-directional-and-partial-derivatives]],
[[def-jacobian-matrix-and-gradient]]); the momentum slot of $H$ is
substituted by $p=S_{q}(t,q,\alpha)$. This is exactly the mathematical
Hamilton-Jacobi equation of
[[def-cm-hamilton-jacobi-equation-and-complete-integral]] associated with
the function $H$ on the open set $J'\times U'\times\mathbb R^{m}$, read in
the chart coordinates $(t,q,p)$; the two definitions determine the same
class of functions.

**(c) Dimensions and chart consistency.** The equation forces
$[S]=\mu\ell^{2}\tau^{-1}$ (action): $S_{t}$ has dimension $[S]\tau^{-1}$
and $H$ has dimension $\mu\ell^{2}\tau^{-2}$, while each $S_{q^{a}}$ has
dimension $[S]/\gamma_{a}$ with $\gamma_{a}$ the declared dimension of the
coordinate $q^{a}$ in this chart; the substitution is dimensionally
consistent in every chart because the chart momenta of
[[def-cm12-cotangent-momentum]] have dimension
$\mu\ell^{2}\tau^{-1}\gamma_{a}^{-1}$. In the Cartesian chart all
$\gamma_{a}=\ell$ and $[S]/\ell=\mu\ell\tau^{-1}$, the momentum dimension.

**(d) Status.** The equation is attached to the declared datum: replacing
the chart or the potential representative
changes $H$ by the rules recorded in clause (d) of
[[def-cm12-hamiltonian]] and hence changes the equation, and a solution
family $S$ is a solution for that datum only. On each fixed hyperregular
chart the inverse Legendre map is unique; it is not an independent branch
choice. The item defines a class of
functions; whether a given datum admits solutions, and how solutions
produce curves of the model, is not asserted here. In particular no
existence theorem, no global solution, no equation of motion for the model,
no conservation law and no measured value is claimed.
items.physical_scope: The Hamilton-Jacobi equation of a declared hyperregular potential presentation of the framework's force branch, read in one of the presentation's momentum charts: the class of $C^3$ functions $S$ of the chart variables $(t,q,\alpha)$ that satisfy $S_t+H(t,q,S_q)=0$ for the branch Hamiltonian $H$ of that chart, together with the action dimension of $S$ and the dependence of the equation on the declared chart, inverse Legendre branch and potential representative. The item defines a function class relative to that datum; it asserts no existence of solutions, no equation of motion for the model, no completeness of any flow and no measured value.

items.title: A complete integral of the model's Hamilton-Jacobi equation: nondegenerate mixed derivative, momentum map and Jacobi constants
items.statement:
Adopt the datum of [[def-cm14-hamilton-jacobi-equation]]: one momentum chart
of a hyperregular potential presentation, its $C^{2}$ Hamiltonian $H$ of
dimension $\mu\ell^{2}\tau^{-2}$ on $I_{0}\times V\times\mathbb R^{m}$, open
sets $J'\subseteq I_{0}$, $U'\subseteq V$ and $A'\subseteq\mathbb R^{m}$,
and a $C^{3}$ map $S:J'\times U'\times A'\to\mathbb R$ that solves the
Hamilton-Jacobi equation associated with $H$ on $J'\times U'\times A'$.
Dimensions are read by [[def-cm01-units]] and differentiability classes are
those of [[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]].

**(a) Complete integral.** Let $(t_{0},q_{0},\alpha_{0})\in
J'\times U'\times A'$. The solution $S$ is a **complete integral of the
model's Hamilton-Jacobi equation at $(t_{0},q_{0},\alpha_{0})$** when the
mixed derivative

$$S_{q\alpha}(t,q,\alpha):=\Bigl(\frac{\partial^{2}S}{\partial q^{a}\partial\alpha_{j}}(t,q,\alpha)\Bigr)_{a,j=1}^{m}\in\mathbb R^{m\times m}$$
is invertible at the base point, $\det S_{q\alpha}(t_{0},q_{0},\alpha_{0})
\ne0$ ([[def-determinant-of-a-square-matrix]],
[[def-invertible-euclidean-linear-map]], mixed partials being those of
[[def-total-derivative-in-euclidean-space]]). This is exactly the
mathematical notion of a complete integral of
[[def-cm-hamilton-jacobi-equation-and-complete-integral]] applied to the
function $H$ on the chart domain $J'\times U'\times\mathbb R^{m}$.

**(b) Parameters and their dimensions.** The third variable
$\alpha=(\alpha_{1},\dots,\alpha_{m})$ is read with the declared coordinate
dimensions $\gamma_{a}$ of $q$ in the fixed chart,
$[\alpha_{j}]=\gamma_{j}$. With this reading the entries of
$S_{q\alpha}$ have dimensions $\mu\ell^{2}\tau^{-1}/(\gamma_a\gamma_j)$.
In Cartesian length coordinates these are mass/time dimensions.
Changing units rescales rows and columns by nonzero factors, so
invertibility is unit-independent; the momentum map below carries the
momentum dimension.

**(c) Momentum map and Jacobi constants.** For a complete integral $S$ the
**momentum map** and the **Jacobi constants** of $S$ are the maps

$$p(t,q,\alpha):=S_{q}(t,q,\alpha),\qquad\beta(t,q,\alpha):=S_{\alpha}(t,q,\alpha),$$
so that $p$ has the chart-momentum dimensions of
[[def-cm12-cotangent-momentum]], $[p_{a}]=\mu\ell^{2}\tau^{-1}
\gamma_{a}^{-1}$, and $\beta$ has the same dimensions as $p$,
$[\beta_{j}]=\mu\ell^{2}\tau^{-1}\gamma_{j}^{-1}$: the product
$\beta_{j}\,\alpha_{j}$ has the action dimension $\mu\ell^{2}\tau^{-1}$ of
$S$. The pair $(\beta,\alpha)$ is the **Jacobi data** of the complete
integral at the base point.

**(d) Status.** The item defines data attached to the presentation and to
the chosen solution. It asserts neither that a complete integral exists
for a given presentation, nor that its characteristic curves are motions
of the model, nor that $\beta$ is constant along such curves; those are
the claims of the page's characteristics theorem. It also
asserts no global statement: $\det S_{q\alpha}\ne0$ is required at the
base point only, and the theorem below records its local consequences.
items.physical_scope: The complete-integral datum of a declared hyperregular potential presentation of the framework's force branch: a $C^3$ solution $S$ of the presentation's Hamilton-Jacobi equation in a fixed momentum chart whose mixed derivative $S_{q\alpha}$ is invertible at the base point, together with its momentum map $p=S_q$ and its Jacobi constants $\beta=S_\alpha$, their dimensions and their reading as a family of model data labelled by the parameters $\alpha$. The item defines the datum only; the constancy of the Jacobi constants along the characteristic motions, the local solvability of the constants equation and the canonicity of $(\beta,\alpha)$ are theorems of this page, not part of the definition, and no existence or measured value is asserted.

items.title: First integrals of the model's Hamiltonian and families in involution: the bracket criterion and differential independence
items.statement:
Adopt the force model with potential presentation $(U,d)$ and mechanical
Lagrangian $L=K-U$ of [[def-cm07-action-and-mechanical-lagrangian]], with
the momentum charts and two-form datum of [[def-cm13-two-form]], the
Hamiltonian fields of [[def-cm13-hamiltonian-field]], the bracket of
[[def-cm13-poisson]] and the branch Hamiltonian $H$ of
[[def-cm12-hamiltonian]], writing $H$ for the Hamiltonian of the
chosen chart ($\widetilde H$ in generalized coordinates). The model
reading is [[pthm-cm13-hamiltonian-field-integrates-the-model-equations]]:
when $d\equiv0$, Cartesian solutions are model motions; generalized-coordinate
solutions satisfy the substituted Lagrange equations. An arbitrary
lower-dimensional immersion alone does not identify those solutions with
ambient unconstrained motions. Dimensions are read by
[[def-cm01-units]] and differentiability classes are those of
[[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]].

**(a) Phase functions and the domain.** Let $W_{0}$ be a nonempty open
subset of one momentum phase domain of the presentation. A **phase
function of the presentation on $W_{0}$ of class $C^{k}$** is a map
$f:W_{0}\to\mathbb R$ of class $C^{k}$, of a declared dimension.

**(b) First integrals.** Let $f:W_{0}\to\mathbb R$ be of class $C^{1}$.
Then $f$ is a **first integral of the branch Hamiltonian $H$ on $W_{0}$**
when for every interval $J\subseteq I_{0}$ with nonempty interior and every
solution $z:J\to W_{0}$ of the Hamiltonian system
$\dot z(t)=X_{H_{t}}(z(t))$
([[def-first-order-ode-initial-value-problem-and-solution]]) the composite
$t\mapsto f(z(t))$ is constant on $J$. In the Cartesian chart with $d\equiv0$, this is equivalently constancy
along every model motion whose momentum-phase curve lies in $W_{0}$, by
clause 1 of [[pthm-cm13-hamiltonian-field-integrates-the-model-equations]].
In generalized coordinates with $d\equiv0$, the same definition concerns
solutions of the substituted Lagrange equations, by its clause 2.

**(c) The bracket criterion.** Let $H$ be autonomous on $I_{0}\times W_{0}$
($\partial_{t}U\equiv0$ and $d\equiv0$) and let $f:W_{0}\to\mathbb R$ be
autonomous of class $C^{2}$. Then $f$ is a first integral of $H$ on $W_{0}$
if and only if

$$\{f,H\}=0\qquad\text{everywhere on }W_{0},$$

the bracket being that of [[def-cm13-poisson]]. For sufficiency, clause 2 of [[pthm-cm13-observable-evolution]] makes
$f\circ z$ constant on every solution when the bracket vanishes. For
necessity, fix $w\in W_{0}$ and a time $t_{*}$ in the interior of $I_{0}$.
The chart field $X_H=(H_p,-H_q)$ is $C^{1}$, hence locally Lipschitz
in state, since the chart Hamiltonian is $C^{2}$. Applying
[[thm-picard-lindelof-local-existence-and-uniqueness]] on the open domain
$\operatorname{int}(I_{0})\times W_{0}$ gives a local Hamiltonian solution
$z$ through $z(t_{*})=w$. If $f$ is a first integral, differentiating the
constant composite at $t_{*}$ and using clause 1 of
[[pthm-cm13-observable-evolution]] gives
$0=(f\circ z)'(t_{*})=\{f,H\}(w)$. This holds for every $w$.

**(d) Involution.** Phase functions $f_{1},\dots,f_{k}:W_{0}\to\mathbb R$
of class $C^{2}$ are **in involution** (or **pairwise Poisson-commuting**)
when

$$\{f_{i},f_{j}\}=0\qquad\text{on }W_{0}\text{ for all }i,j\in\{1,\dots,k\};$$

a **family of first integrals in involution** is a family whose members are
first integrals of $H$ and which is in involution. The notion is the
presentation reading of the root-library notion of
[[def-first-integral-and-poisson-commuting-functions]] under the bracket of
[[def-cm13-poisson]], which is the bracket of
[[def-poisson-bracket-on-a-symplectic-manifold]] for the two-form of
[[def-cm13-two-form]].

**(e) Differential independence.** Phase functions $f_{1},\dots,f_{k}$ of
class $C^{1}$ are **independent at $z\in W_{0}$** when the differentials
$df_{1}(z),\dots,df_{k}(z)$ are linearly independent as elements of the
dual of the tangent space at $z$ ([[def-linear-independence]]); the set
of points at which this holds is the **independence locus** of the family,
$\{z\in W_{0}:\operatorname{rank}(df_{1}(z),\dots,df_{k}(z))=k\}$
([[def-differential-rank-and-constant-rank]],
[[def-jacobian-matrix-and-gradient]]). The family is **independent on**
$W_{0}$ when it is independent at every $z\in W_{0}$.

**(f) Status.** The item defines model properties of phase functions and
establishes the bracket equivalence using observable evolution and
local existence through every phase point. It asserts no existence of a nonconstant first integral
for a given force law, no completeness of any flow, no conservation law
of the model and no measured value; in particular every closure or
constancy statement about brackets is a theorem of this page or of
[[pthm-cm13-observable-evolution]], not part of the definition.
items.physical_scope: First integrals and involution for the Hamiltonian system of a declared hyperregular potential presentation of the framework's force branch: phase functions on an open phase domain that are constant along Hamiltonian solutions, their bracket criterion with the branch Hamiltonian, families of phase functions in involution, and the differential independence of a family on the regular region. The item defines these model properties; it asserts no existence of integrals, no conservation law for a particular force law and no measured value.

items.title: Completely integrable data of a declared presentation: $n$ smooth phase functions with $F_1=H$, pairwise in involution and independent on the regular locus
items.statement:
Adopt the force model with potential presentation $(U,d)$ and mechanical
Lagrangian $L=K-U$ of [[def-cm07-action-and-mechanical-lagrangian]], with
the momentum charts and two-form datum of [[def-cm13-two-form]], the
canonical coordinates of [[def-cm13-canonical-form]], the bracket of
[[def-cm13-poisson]], the Hamiltonian fields of [[def-cm13-hamiltonian-field]] and the Hamiltonian of the chosen chart of [[def-cm12-hamiltonian]]:
$H$ in Cartesian coordinates or $\widetilde H$ in generalized coordinates.
Assume this chart Hamiltonian is autonomous and write it throughout this
definition as $H:W\to\mathbb R$, on that same chart's phase domain $W$;
by clauses 1–2 of [[pthm-cm13-two-form-is-symplectic]] (clause 1 for the
Cartesian domain and clause 2 for a generalized-coordinate domain), each momentum phase
domain is a symplectic manifold for $\omega$, with $\omega$ the standard
two-form in the chart's canonical coordinates
([[def-symplectic-form-and-symplectic-manifold]]). Dimensions are read by
[[def-cm01-units]] and differentiability classes are those of
[[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]].

**(a) The datum.** Let $W_{0}$ be a nonempty open subset of one momentum
phase domain of the presentation, of dimension $2n$, and let

$$F=(F_{1},\dots,F_{n}),\qquad F_{i}:W_{0}\longrightarrow\mathbb R,$$

be phase functions of class $C^{\infty}$ with $F_{1}=H|_{W_{0}}$. The
family $F$ is a **completely integrable datum of the presentation on
$W_{0}$** when

1. $F$ is in involution, $\{F_{i},F_{j}\}=0$ on $W_{0}$ for all $i,j$
   ([[def-cm14-involution]] clause (d)); and
2. the differentials $dF_{1},\dots,dF_{n}$ are linearly independent on a
   dense open subset of $W_{0}$ ([[def-linear-independence]],
   [[def-differential-rank-and-constant-rank]]).

**(b) Reading in the root library.** Since $(W_{0},\omega)$ is a
$2n$-dimensional symplectic manifold and the bracket of
[[def-cm13-poisson]] is the bracket of
[[def-poisson-bracket-on-a-symplectic-manifold]] for $\omega$, a datum
$F$ in the sense of clause (a), with $F_{1}=H$ and the autonomous
Hamiltonian $H$ of the presentation, is exactly a **completely integrable
Hamiltonian system** on $(W_{0},\omega)$ in the sense of
[[def-completely-integrable-hamiltonian-system]], with branches read
through the presentation's Hamiltonians; the root notion of
[[def-first-integral-and-poisson-commuting-functions]] is read through the
bracket criterion of [[def-cm14-involution]] clause (c), whose sufficiency
is [[pthm-cm13-observable-evolution]] clause 2.

**(c) Integral map, regular locus and fibres.** Attached to a datum $F$
are:

1. the **integral map** $F:W_{0}\to\mathbb R^{n}$;
2. the **regular locus** $W_{\mathrm{reg}}:=\{z\in W_{0}:
   \operatorname{rank}dF(z)=n\}$, which is open by continuity of the partial
   derivatives and dense in $W_{0}$ by clause (a) 2;
3. the **regular values**, namely the values $b\in F(W_{0})$ such that
   $\operatorname{rank}dF(z)=n$ at every $z\in F^{-1}(b)$;
   for such a value the **regular fibre** $N_{b}:=F^{-1}(b)$ is the
   common level set of $F_{1},\dots,F_{n}$ through $b$;
4. the **Hamiltonian fields** $X_{F_{1}},\dots,X_{F_{n}}$ of the family
   ([[def-cm13-hamiltonian-field]]).

**(d) Status.** The item defines a datum class and its attached objects.
It makes no assertion that a particular model is completely integrable,
that a fibre is compact, connected or a torus, that action-angle coordinates
exist, or that a measured value is known; the
structural and motion statements are the torus theorem and the
action-angle theorem of this page (items `pthm-cm14-regular-tori` and
`pthm-cm14-action-angle`), conditional on the hypotheses stated there.
items.physical_scope: Complete integrability of the Hamiltonian system of a declared hyperregular potential presentation: a datum of $n$ phase functions on an open phase domain of dimension $2n$, with first entry the autonomous branch Hamiltonian, pairwise in involution, independent on an open dense regular locus, and the attached integral map, regular values and regular fibres; the datum is a completely integrable Hamiltonian system for the presentation's two-form in the root-library sense. The item defines the datum class without asserting complete integrability of any particular model, any fibre structure, existence of action-angle coordinates or any measured value.

items.title: A complete integral of the model's Hamilton-Jacobi equation produces chart Hamiltonian characteristics, Jacobi constants and local canonical $(\beta,\alpha)$ labels
items.statement:
Adopt the force model with potential presentation $(U,d)$ and mechanical
Lagrangian $L=K-U$ of [[def-cm07-action-and-mechanical-lagrangian]] with the
data and conventions of [[def-cm12-cotangent-momentum]]: masses
$m_{1},\dots,m_{N}>0$, open configuration domain $Q\subseteq\mathbb R^{3N}$,
time window $I_{0}$, mass operator $\mathsf M$
([[def-cm01-configuration]]), $C^{2}$ potential $U$ and residual forces $d$
of the standing regularity ([[def-cm03-potential-and-mechanical-energy]],
[[post-cm02-force-superposition]]), the presentation being hyperregular on
its charts ([[pthm-cm12-mechanical-hyperregularity]],
[[def-cm12-hamiltonian]]). Fix one momentum chart of the presentation
(Cartesian coordinates $(t,x,p)$, or the chart $(t,q,p)$ of a
generalized-coordinate map $X:\Omega\to Q$
([[def-cm07-generalized-coordinates-and-forces]])), with $m$ pairs of
coordinates and Hamiltonian $H$ of class $C^{2}$ on
$J_{0}\times V\times\mathbb R^{m}$; let $S:J\times U\times A\to\mathbb R$
be a $C^{3}$ complete integral of the model's Hamilton-Jacobi equation at
$(t_{0},q_{0},\alpha_{0})\in J\times U\times A$ in the sense of
[[def-cm14-hamilton-jacobi-equation]] and [[def-cm14-complete-integral]]
($J\subseteq J_{0}$, $U\subseteq V$, $A\subseteq\mathbb R^{m}$ open), and
put

$$\beta_{0}:=S_{\alpha}(t_{0},q_{0},\alpha_{0}).$$

Then:

1. **(characteristic curves)** For every $\alpha$ sufficiently close to
   $\alpha_{0}$ there is an open interval $I_{\alpha}\ni t_{0}$ and a
   $C^{1}$ curve $q:I_{\alpha}\to U$ with $q(t_{0})=q_{0}$ solving
   $q'(t)=H_{p}\bigl(t,q(t),S_{q}(t,q(t),\alpha)\bigr)$, and with
   $p(t):=S_{q}(t,q(t),\alpha)$ the pair $(q,p)$ satisfies Hamilton's
   equations $q'=H_{p}$, $p'=-H_{q}$ on $I_{\alpha}$. If the chart is the
   Cartesian chart and $d\equiv0$ on the state domain, then $x:=q$ is a
   motion of the model on $I_{\alpha}$ and $p(t)=\mathsf Mx'(t)$
   ([[def-cm02-newtonian-flow]], [[def-cm12-cotangent-momentum]]); if the
   chart is the chart of a generalized-coordinate map and $d\equiv0$, then
   $q$ solves the declared Lagrange equations of the substituted
   Lagrangian and $p(t)=G(q(t))q'(t)$
   ([[def-cm07-generalized-coordinates-and-forces]],
   [[pthm-cm12-hamilton-equivalence]]).
2. **(Jacobi constants)** With $(q,p)$ as in clause 1,
   $\beta(t):=S_{\alpha}(t,q(t),\alpha)$ is constant on $I_{\alpha}$ and
   equal to $S_{\alpha}(t_{0},q_{0},\alpha)$.
3. **(local converse)** For $(\alpha,\beta)$ sufficiently close to
   $(\alpha_{0},\beta_{0})$ the equation $\beta=S_{\alpha}(t,q,\alpha)$
   can be solved locally for $q=Q(t,\alpha,\beta)$, and with
   $p:=S_{q}\bigl(t,Q(t,\alpha,\beta),\alpha\bigr)$ the curve
   $t\mapsto(Q,p)$ solves Hamilton's equations; in the Cartesian chart on
   the potential branch it is the momentum-phase curve of a motion of the
   model.
4. **(canonical labels)** On the domain of the local diffeomorphism
   $(q,p)\mapsto(\beta,\alpha)$ obtained by composing
   $(q,p)\mapsto(q,\alpha)$ (solving $p=S_{q}$) with
   $(q,\alpha)\mapsto(\beta,\alpha)$, one has
   $\omega=d\beta\wedge d\alpha$ at every fixed $t$, where $\omega$ is the
   two-form of the presentation in this chart
   ([[def-cm13-two-form]]); equivalently, $(\beta,\alpha)$ are canonical
   coordinates of the presentation in the sense of clause (a) of
   [[def-cm13-canonical-form]].
items.physical_scope: The characteristics theorem of the Hamilton-Jacobi method for a declared hyperregular potential presentation of the framework's force branch: from a complete integral of the presentation's Hamilton-Jacobi equation in a fixed momentum chart, the characteristic curves of the equation solve the chart's Hamilton equations; when $dquiv0$, Cartesian characteristics are motions of the model and generalized-coordinate characteristics solve the substituted Lagrange equations; the derivatives of the complete integral in the parameters are constant along them; a local converse solves the constants equation for the configuration; and the Jacobi data are local canonical coordinates of the presentation's two-form. The statement is a conditional deduction from the adopted force branch, the declared presentation and the cited mathematics; it is local in the time, configuration and parameter variables, assumes the nondegeneracy of the mixed derivative at the base point only, and asserts no global solution, no completeness and no empirical content.

items.title: Compact connected regular fibres of a completely integrable datum of the presentation are Lagrangian tori with a full period lattice
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_{\omega}$
([[def-countable-choice]]). Adopt the force model with potential
presentation $(U,d)$ and mechanical Lagrangian $L=K-U$ of
[[def-cm07-action-and-mechanical-lagrangian]], with the momentum charts and
two-form datum of [[def-cm13-two-form]], the Hamiltonian fields of
[[def-cm13-hamiltonian-field]] and the branch Hamiltonian $H$ of
[[def-cm12-hamiltonian]]; by clauses 1–2 of
[[pthm-cm13-two-form-is-symplectic]] (clause 1 for Cartesian domains and
clause 2 for generalized-coordinate domains), each momentum phase domain is a
symplectic manifold for the presentation's two-form $\omega$
([[def-symplectic-form-and-symplectic-manifold]]). Let $W_{0}\subseteq W$
be a nonempty open phase domain of dimension $2n$ and let
$F=(F_{1}=H|_{W_{0}},\dots,F_{n})$ be a completely integrable datum of the
presentation on $W_{0}$ ([[def-cm14-complete-integrability]]). Let $b_{0}$
be a regular value of the integral map whose regular fibre
$N:=F^{-1}(b_{0})\subseteq W_{0}$ is nonempty, compact and connected, and
assume there are a saturated open neighbourhood $U\subseteq W_{0}$ of $N$
and a ball $B\subseteq\mathbb R^{n}$ of regular values with $F(U)=B$ such
that $\pi:=F|_{U}:U\to B$ is a proper submersion with connected fibres.
Then:

1. **(Lagrangian fibre)** $N$ is a compact connected embedded
   $n$-dimensional Lagrangian submanifold of $(W_{0},\omega)$, and for
   every $z\in N$
   $$T_{z}N=\operatorname{span}\{X_{F_{1}}(z),\dots,X_{F_{n}}(z)\},$$
   the fields being those of [[def-cm13-hamiltonian-field]].
2. **(commuting flows and period lattice)** The fields
   $X_{F_{1}},\dots,X_{F_{n}}$ have pairwise commuting flows; these flows
   combine into a local $\mathbb R^{n}$ action on $W_{\mathrm{reg}}$, and
   on the compact invariant fibre $N$ their restrictions are complete and
   generate a transitive action of $\mathbb R^{n}$ whose stabilizer at
   every point is one and the same full lattice $\Gamma\subseteq
   \mathbb R^{n}$, with $N\cong\mathbb R^{n}/\Gamma$.
3. **(torus)** $N$ is diffeomorphic to the torus
   $T^{n}=\mathbb R^{n}/\mathbb Z^{n}$.

The statement is conditional on the adopted force branch, the declared
presentation, the smooth completely integrable datum and the listed
hypotheses on the fibre; it asserts no global product structure of $U$, no
action-angle coordinates, no completeness of any flow outside the compact
fibre and no empirical content.
items.physical_scope: The fibre structure of a completely integrable datum of a declared hyperregular potential presentation of the framework's force branch: a compact connected regular common fibre of the integral map is an embedded Lagrangian submanifold generically spanned by the datum's Hamiltonian fields, carries the commuting-field local action of the cited mathematics as a transitive complete action with a full stabilizer lattice, and is diffeomorphic to a torus. The conclusion is conditional on the datum's smoothness, involution, independence on the regular locus, the compactness, connectedness and regularity of the fibre, and on the Axiom of Countable Choice through the cited lattice lemma; it asserts no global fibration, no action-angle coordinates, no completeness of flows off the compact fibre and no empirical content.

items.title: Action-angle coordinates of a completely integrable presentation: period-one angles, action coordinates, $H=h(I)$ and linear motion on the tori
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_{\omega}$
([[def-countable-choice]]). Adopt the force model with potential
presentation $(U,d)$ and mechanical Lagrangian $L=K-U$ of
[[def-cm07-action-and-mechanical-lagrangian]], with the momentum charts,
forms and canonical coordinates of [[def-cm13-two-form]],
[[pthm-cm13-two-form-is-symplectic]] and [[def-cm13-canonical-form]], the
Hamiltonian fields of [[def-cm13-hamiltonian-field]], the bracket of
[[def-cm13-poisson]] and the branch Hamiltonian $H$ of
[[def-cm12-hamiltonian]]. Let $W_{0}$ be a nonempty open phase domain of a
momentum chart, of dimension $2n$, and let $F=(F_{1}=H|_{W_{0}},\dots,F_{n})$
be a completely integrable datum of the presentation on $W_{0}$
([[def-cm14-complete-integrability]]). Let $b_{0}$ be a regular value with
nonempty compact connected regular fibre $N=F^{-1}(b_{0})$, and assume
that there are a saturated open neighbourhood $U\subseteq W_{0}$ of $N$
and a ball $B\subseteq\mathbb R^{n}$ of regular values with $F(U)=B$ such
that $\pi=F|_{U}:U\to B$ is a proper submersion with connected fibres.
Then there are an open base neighbourhood $B_0\subseteq B$ of $b_0$ and an open action-coordinate ball $A$, and on the saturated neighbourhood $U_0:=\pi^{-1}(B_0)$ there are action-angle coordinates

$$(I,\theta):U_0\longrightarrow A\times T^{n},\qquad T^{n}=\mathbb R^{n}/\mathbb Z^{n},$$

of class $C^{\infty}$, diffeomorphic onto their image, such that:

1. **(form)** the angles are period-one and the presentation's two-form
   takes the canonical action-angle form
   $$\omega=\sum_{i=1}^{n}d\theta_{i}\wedge dI_{i}$$
   on $U_0$, in the sense of [[def-action-and-angle-coordinates]];
2. **(dimension)** each action coordinate $I_{i}$ has dimension
   $\mu\ell^{2}\tau^{-1}$ (action) and each angle $\theta_{i}$ is
   dimensionless, consistently with the action dimension of the
   presentation's two-form in its original canonical charts
   ([[def-cm01-units]]);
3. **(fibrewise constants)** every $C^{\infty}$ function on $U_0$ that is
   constant on the fibres of $\pi$ is a function of $I$ alone; in
   particular $F_{i}=f_{i}(I)$ for $C^{\infty}$ functions $f_{i}$ and the
   branch Hamiltonian is $H=h(I)$ with $h=f_{1}$;
4. **(linear motion)** the solutions of the Hamiltonian system of $h$ in
   the chart $(I,\theta)$, on the potential branch $d\equiv0$, are exactly
   the momentum-phase curves of Cartesian model motions, or in a
   generalized-coordinate chart the solutions of its substituted Lagrange
   equations on $U_0$, by clauses 1-2 of
   [[pthm-cm13-hamiltonian-field-integrates-the-model-equations]].
   A lower-dimensional immersion requires a separate ideal-constraint
   premise to identify these with constrained ambient motions. In either case
   and they satisfy
$$\dot I=0,\qquad \dot\theta=\frac{\partial h}{\partial I}(I),\qquad\theta(t)=\theta(0)+t\,\frac{\partial h}{\partial I}\bigl(I(0)\bigr)\pmod{\mathbb Z^{n}},$$
   writing $\nu=\partial h/\partial I(I(0))$, a positive $T$ is a period exactly when $T\nu\in\mathbb Z^n$. The linear-motion formula alone does not assert a periodic-versus-full-density dichotomy: nonperiodic motion can remain in a proper invariant subtorus when the frequency vector has integer relations.
5. **(radian rescaling)** with the rescaled coordinates
   $\theta^{\mathrm{rad}}:=2\pi\theta$ and
   $I^{\mathrm{rad}}:=I/(2\pi)$ one has
   $\omega=\sum_{i}d\theta^{\mathrm{rad}}_{i}\wedge dI^{\mathrm{rad}}_{i}$,
   the angles $\theta^{\mathrm{rad}}$ are $2\pi$-periodic, and
   $H=\tilde h(I^{\mathrm{rad}})$ with
   $\tilde h(I^{\mathrm{rad}})=h(2\pi I^{\mathrm{rad}})$ and
   $\dot\theta^{\mathrm{rad}}=\partial\tilde h/\partial I^{\mathrm{rad}}$;
   the components $\partial h/\partial I_{i}$ are **cyclic frequencies**
   (cycles per unit time), not angular rates, the angular rates being
   $2\pi\,\partial h/\partial I_{i}$.

The statement is conditional on the adopted force branch, the declared
presentation, the smooth completely integrable datum, the fibre
hypotheses and $\mathrm{AC}_{\omega}$; it asserts no global
action-angle coordinates on $W_{0}$, no statement about critical or
noncompact fibres and no empirical content.
items.physical_scope: Action-angle coordinates for a completely integrable datum of a declared hyperregular potential presentation of the framework's force branch: near a compact connected regular fibre and over a ball of regular values on which the integral map is a proper submersion with connected fibres, there are period-one angle and action coordinates of the presentation's two-form with $\omega=\sum_i d\theta_i\wedge dI_i$; fibrewise-constant functions, in particular the datum and the branch Hamiltonian, depend on the actions alone; and, with zero residual force, Hamiltonian solutions become constant-action, linear-angle flows: these correspond to Cartesian model motions or, in generalized coordinates, to substituted Lagrange solutions; a lower-dimensional immersion alone does not make the latter ambient unconstrained motions. The conclusion is conditional on the Axiom of Countable Choice, on the complete integrability of the datum and on all the fibre hypotheses; it is local over the ball of regular values, asserts no global coordinates on the phase domain, and carries no empirical content. The identification of the coordinates with classical period integrals is a normalization convention, not part of the theorem.

items.title: Adiabatic invariance of the action of a slowly varying one-frequency model: an order-$\varepsilon$ drift bound on the $O(1/\varepsilon)$ time scale
items.statement:
Adopt the force model with potential presentation $(U,d)$ and mechanical
Lagrangian $L=K-U$ of [[def-cm07-action-and-mechanical-lagrangian]], with
the momentum charts and canonical coordinates of [[def-cm13-two-form]],
[[pthm-cm13-two-form-is-symplectic]] and [[def-cm13-canonical-form]], the
Hamiltonian fields of [[def-cm13-hamiltonian-field]] and the branch
Hamiltonian $H$ of [[def-cm12-hamiltonian]]. Fix one momentum chart and
let $(I,\theta)$ be a fixed, time-independent one-degree-of-freedom canonical chart of the presentation on an open set
$U$ of that phase domain, with radian angles and
$\omega=d\theta\wedge dI$ there, obtained from the period-one chart of [[pthm-cm14-action-angle]] by
$\theta^{\mathrm{rad}}=2\pi\theta^{\mathrm{one}}$,
$I^{\mathrm{rad}}=I^{\mathrm{one}}/(2\pi)$ as in
[[cor-cm-action-angle-radian-scaling]], suppressing the radian superscripts; $I$ has the
action dimension of clause 2 of that theorem. Use the dimensions of
[[def-cm01-units]]: $[t]=\tau$, $[I]=\mu\ell^2\tau^{-1}$,
$[\theta]=[s]=[s_0]=[A]=1$, $[\varepsilon]=[\omega_0]=\tau^{-1}$,
$[h]=[K_s]=\mu\ell^2\tau^{-2}$ and $[k]=\mu\ell^2\tau^{-1}$.
Thus $\varepsilon$ is the prescribed slow parameter rate, $A$ is the
dimensionless parameter excursion, and $A/\varepsilon$ is a duration.
Let $\varepsilon,A,\omega_0>0$ have these dimensions. Let
$\widehat J,\widehat S\subseteq\mathbb R$ be open intervals, and let
$J\subseteq\widehat J$ and $S\subseteq\widehat S$ be intervals with nonempty interiors
([[def-interval]]), let $K\subseteq J$ and $S_{0}\subseteq S$ be compact
intervals, let $s_{0}\in S_{0}$, and let

$$h:\widehat J\times\widehat S\longrightarrow\mathbb R,\qquad k:\widehat J\times\mathbb R\times\widehat S\longrightarrow\mathbb R$$
be of class $C^{2}$ on these open domains, with $k$ $2\pi$-periodic in its second variable on $J\times\mathbb R\times S$
([[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]]). Suppose:

1. **(slow datum)** for every parameter value $s\in S$ and every
   $(I,\theta)\in J\times\mathbb R$ in the chart, the branch Hamiltonian
   of the model restricted to the chart is
   $$K_{s}(I,\theta)=h(I,s)+\varepsilon\,k(I,\theta,s);$$
2. **(nonvanishing frequency)** $|\partial_{I}h(I,s)|\ge\omega_{0}$ for
   all $(I,s)\in K\times S_{0}$;
3. **(parameter path and solution)** $s(t):=s_{0}+\varepsilon t$, and
   $t\mapsto(I(t),\theta(t))$ on $[0,A/\varepsilon]$ is the chart
   expression of a motion of the model (on the potential branch, under
   the identification of clause 4 of [[pthm-cm14-action-angle]]) satisfying
   $I(t)\in K$ and $s(t)\in S_{0}$ for every $t\in[0,A/\varepsilon]$.

Then for every $t\in[0,A/\varepsilon]$,

$$|I(t)-I(0)|\le\varepsilon\Bigl[2\sup_{K\times[0,2\pi]\times S_{0}}|g|+A\sup_{K\times[0,2\pi]\times S_{0}}\bigl|\partial_{I}g\,\partial_{\theta}k-\partial_{\theta}g\,\partial_{I}k-\partial_{s}g\bigr|\Bigr],$$
where $g=(k-\langle k\rangle)/\partial_{I}h$ is the drift generator and
$\langle k\rangle(I,s)=\frac1{2\pi}\int_{0}^{2\pi}k(I,\theta,s)\,d\theta$
the angle average of $k$ ([[def-cm-parameter-dependent-action-angle-branch]]).
All partial derivatives are those of the ambient open extensions. The
generator has dimension $[g]=\mu\ell^2$; each term inside the second
supremum has that same dimension, so both terms multiplied by
$\varepsilon$ have action dimension. At the included time endpoints,
derivatives are relative to the nondegenerate interval $[0,A/\varepsilon]$.

The statement is conditional on the adopted force branch, the declared
presentation, the existence of the uniform action-angle chart, the
frequency bound and the trapping hypothesis; it asserts no exact
invariance of the action, no statement for parameter paths that leave the
chart, cross a separatrix or make the frequency vanish, and no empirical
content. In particular the order-$\varepsilon$ bound is a bound on the
stated horizon $[0,A/\varepsilon]$ and is not an asymptotic equivalence.
items.physical_scope: Adiabatic invariance of the action coordinate of a declared hyperregular potential presentation of the framework's force branch when the model carries a slow real parameter: if in a one-degree-of-freedom radian action-angle chart the branch Hamiltonian is $h(I,s)+\varepsilon k(I,\theta,s)$ with nonvanishing frequency $|\partial_Ih|\ge\omega_0$ and the parameter runs as $s(t)=s_0+\varepsilon t$, then along every model solution that stays in the compact chart region the action changes by at most the displayed order-$\varepsilon$ bound on $0\le t\le A/\varepsilon$. The statement uses a dimensionless slow parameter, an inverse-time slow rate, energy-dimension h and action-dimension k; it is conditional on C2 open extension data, a uniform fixed canonical chart for the parameter-dependent Hamiltonian on the zero-residual-force branch, the frequency bound and the trapping of the solution; it asserts no exact invariance, no statement across a separatrix or a chart boundary, and no empirical content.

items.title: Scope of the Hamilton-Jacobi and integrability statements: locality, the fibre hypotheses, global obstructions and the frequency conventions
items.physical_scope: The recorded scope of the Hamilton-Jacobi and integrability items of this page: the local character of the Hamilton-Jacobi construction and of its no-caustic hypothesis; the separate requirements of involution and independence in complete integrability; the compactness, connectedness, regularity and proper-submersion hypotheses of the torus and action-angle conclusions together with their Countable-Choice assumption; the published monodromy obstruction to global action-angle coordinates; and the period-one versus radian frequency convention. The remark asserts no new mathematical claim and no empirical content; it is a scope record for the conditional deductions of this page.

items.title: The harmonic model worked through: an explicit complete integral, its characteristic motion, and the action-angle chart with $I=\oint p\,dx$ and period-one frequency $1/T$
items.statement:
Adopt the harmonic model of [[post-cm04-harmonic-model]]: one label of mass
$m>0$ on $\mathbb R$ with spring constant $k>0$, force law $F(x)=-kx$,
potential $U(x)=\tfrac12kx^{2}$ and no residual force.
For the CM12-CM14 presentation interfaces, declare the ambient one-label
model on $Q_{\mathrm{amb}}=\mathbb R^{3}$ with mass operator $mI_{3}$,
time window $\mathbb R$, potential $U_{\mathrm{amb}}(y)=ky_{1}^{2}/2$,
$d=0$ and smooth force $F_{\mathrm{amb}}(y,v)=(-ky_{1},0,0)$
([[post-cm02-force-superposition]], [[def-cm03-potential-and-mechanical-energy]],
[[def-cm07-action-and-mechanical-lagrangian]]).
The generalized-coordinate map $X:\mathbb R\to Q_{\mathrm{amb}}$,
$X(x)=(x,0,0)$ is a smooth immersion with length-valued coordinate $x$,
$G=DX^{\mathsf T}mI_{3}DX=m$ and substituted potential $kx^{2}/2$
([[def-cm07-generalized-coordinates-and-forces]]).
Thus its chart Hamiltonian $\widetilde H$ of
[[def-cm12-hamiltonian]] clause (b) is exactly the scalar Hamiltonian
below; write it as $H$. A scalar harmonic motion reconstructs an ambient
motion $X\circ x$ since the longitudinal equation is $mx''=-kx$ and
both transverse equations are $0=0$. Write

$$\omega:=\sqrt{\frac{k}{m}}>0,\qquad T:=\frac{2\pi}{\omega},$$

so that $U(x)=\tfrac12m\omega^{2}x^{2}$ and the branch Hamiltonian in the
generalized-coordinate chart is

$$H(x,p)=\frac{p^{2}}{2m}+\frac{m\omega^{2}}{2}x^{2}$$

([[pthm-cm12-mechanical-hyperregularity]], [[def-cm12-hamiltonian]]), with
$[H]=\mu\ell^{2}\tau^{-2}$ ([[def-cm01-units]]). On the open set

$$V:=\{(t,x,\alpha)\in\mathbb R^{3}:\sin(\omega t)\neq0\}$$

define

$$S(t,x,\alpha):=\frac{m\omega}{2}\Bigl[(x^{2}+\alpha^{2})\cot(\omega t)-2x\alpha\,\csc(\omega t)\Bigr].$$
The example checks the following claims of this page on this instance.

1. **(complete integral)** $S$ is of class $C^{\infty}$ on $V$ and solves
   the model's Hamilton-Jacobi equation
   $S_{t}+H(x,S_{x})=0$ on $V$; the mixed derivative is
   $S_{x\alpha}=-m\omega\,\csc(\omega t)$, so $S$ is a complete integral of
   the model's Hamilton-Jacobi equation at every point of $V$
   ([[def-cm14-hamilton-jacobi-equation]],
   [[def-cm14-complete-integral]]).
2. **(characteristics)** for every $(t_{0},x_{0},\alpha_{0})\in V$ and
   every real $\beta$, the curve
   $$x(t)=\alpha_{0}\cos(\omega t)-\frac{\beta}{m\omega}\sin(\omega t)$$
   satisfies $S_{\alpha}(t,x(t),\alpha_{0})=\beta$, and with
   $p(t):=S_{x}(t,x(t),\alpha_{0})$ the pair $(x,p)$ solves
   $x'=H_{p}$, $p'=-H_{x}$ on every interval on which
   $\sin(\omega t)\neq0$; hence $x$ is a motion of the harmonic model with
   $p=mx'$ and $S_{\alpha}$ is constant along it
   ([[pthm-cm14-hamilton-jacobi-characteristics]]).
3. **(action-angle chart)** the map
$$(\theta,I)\longmapsto(x,p)=\Bigl(\sqrt{\frac{I}{\pi m\omega}}\,\sin(2\pi\theta),\ \sqrt{\frac{Im\omega}{\pi}}\,\cos(2\pi\theta)\Bigr)$$

   for $I>0$ and $\theta\in\mathbb R/\mathbb Z$ is a $C^{\infty}$
   parametrization of the punctured phase plane; local real lifts of
   $\theta$ give charts with $\{x,p\}=1$ for the
   presentation's bracket, i.e. a canonical chart of
   [[def-cm13-canonical-form]] with
   $\omega_{\mathrm{form}}=d\theta\wedge dI$ in the period-one convention
   of [[def-action-and-angle-coordinates]], and in it
   $$H=h(I)=\frac{I}{T},$$
   so that every motion satisfies $\dot I=0$,
   $\dot\theta=1/T$, by the canonical Hamiltonian field of
   [[def-cm13-hamiltonian-field]] clause (a).
4. **(action normalization)** the action coordinate is the period integral
   $$I=\oint p\,dx=\int_{0}^{T}p(t)\,x'(t)\,dt$$
   along one period of the oscillator motion, in the period-one
   normalization discussed in the remark of [[pthm-cm14-action-angle]].
5. **(radian convention)** with $\theta^{\mathrm{rad}}:=2\pi\theta$ and
   $I^{\mathrm{rad}}:=I/(2\pi)$ the chart becomes
   $x=\sqrt{2I^{\mathrm{rad}}/(m\omega)}\,\sin\theta^{\mathrm{rad}}$,
   $p=\sqrt{2I^{\mathrm{rad}}m\omega}\,\cos\theta^{\mathrm{rad}}$ with
   $H=\omega I^{\mathrm{rad}}$ and
   $\dot\theta^{\mathrm{rad}}=\omega$, which is the radian chart of the
   sources ([[cor-cm-action-angle-radian-scaling]]).

All data $m,k$ are declared model parameters; the example asserts no
measured value and no claim about a real oscillator.
items.physical_scope: A worked instance of the Hamilton-Jacobi and action-angle items inside the declared scalar harmonic model, identified with the generalized-coordinate presentation of the explicit straight-line immersion into a three-dimensional force model: for one label of mass $m>0$ and spring constant $k>0$, the explicit family $S$ is a complete integral of the model's Hamilton-Jacobi equation wherever $\sin(\omega t)\neq0$; its characteristic curves are the harmonic motions with $\beta=S_\alpha$ constant; and the explicit chart $(\theta,I)$ is canonical with $H=I/T$, $\dot I=0$, $\dot\theta=1/T$ and $I=\oint p\,dx$, in the period-one convention, with the radian rescaling recovering the sources' chart. The example asserts no measured value, no claim that a real oscillator realizes the model, and no global extension of $S$ across the conjugate times $\omega t\in\pi\mathbb Z$.

items.title: The gravitational two-body model on an elliptic orbit: two simple turning points of the effective potential and $J_{\mathrm a}'(E)=T/(2\pi)=\sqrt{\mu/\kappa}\,a^{3/2}$
items.statement:
Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ ([[def-countable-choice]]), as required by the conic, ellipse and period suppliers.

Adopt the two-label gravitational model of [[post-cm05-gravity]] clause (i)
inside the central-force model of [[post-cm05-central-model]]: inertial
masses $m_{1},m_{2}>0$, $M=m_{1}+m_{2}$, reduced mass
$\mu=m_{1}m_{2}/M$, gravitational couplings $m_{1}^{g},m_{2}^{g}>0$,
$\kappa=G_{\mathrm N}m_{1}^{g}m_{2}^{g}>0$ and the pair potential of
[[pthm-cm05-relative-reduction]]. Let $x:I\to Q$ be a motion whose
relative coordinate $r$ has constant angular momentum $j=Je_{3}$ with
$J>0$ and constant energy $E<0$. Let $\bar r:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R^{3}\setminus\{0\}$ be the unique global central-force extension of $r$ supplied by [[thm-cm-kepler-orbit-period]] clause 1 and [[pthm-cm05-kepler-period]] clause 1. In all subsequent period and quadrature statements, write $r:=\bar r$, $\rho:=|\bar r|$ and let $\theta:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ be its increasing polar-angle lift. Its restriction to the initial interval is the original relative motion; no global physical time window is assumed. Let $0\le e<1$, $\theta_{0}$,

$$p=\frac{J^{2}}{\mu\kappa},\qquad a=\frac{p}{1-e^{2}},\qquad b=a\sqrt{1-e^{2}},\qquad T=2\pi\sqrt{\frac{\mu}{\kappa}}\,a^{3/2}$$
be its conic data ([[thm-cm-kepler-conic-and-eccentricity]],
[[pthm-cm05-kepler-period]]). Write

$$I_{0}:=\left(-\frac{\mu\kappa^{2}}{2J^{2}},\,0\right),\qquad r_{*}:=\frac{J^{2}}{\mu\kappa}=p,\qquad U^{\mathrm{eff}}(\rho):=-\frac{\kappa}{\rho}+\frac{J^{2}}{2\mu\rho^{2}}\quad(\rho>0)$$
for the effective potential of [[pthm-cm05-effective-potential]] (its
effective potential $U^{\mathrm{eff}}_{J}$). The example verifies:

1. **(two simple turning points)** $U^{\mathrm{eff}}$ is of class
   $C^{\infty}$ on $(0,\infty)$, has the unique critical point $r_{*}$
   with $U^{\mathrm{eff}}(r_{*})=-\mu\kappa^{2}/(2J^{2})$, is strictly
   decreasing on $(0,r_{*})$ and strictly increasing on $(r_{*},\infty)$;
   hence for every $E\in I_{0}$ there are exactly two solutions
   $0<r_{-}(E)<r_{*}<r_{+}(E)$ of $U^{\mathrm{eff}}(\rho)=E$, with
   $(U^{\mathrm{eff}})'(r_{-}(E))<0<(U^{\mathrm{eff}})'(r_{+}(E))$ and
   $U^{\mathrm{eff}}<E$ between them, and the datum
   $(J_{0},U^{\mathrm{eff}},\mu)$ with $J_{0}=(0,\infty)$ satisfies the
   hypotheses of [[thm-cm-action-variable-derivative]] on the energy
   window $I_{0}$.
2. **(action derivative)** consequently the action variable
   $J_{\mathrm a}$ of [[def-cm-one-dimensional-action-variable]] is of
   class $C^{1}$ on $I_{0}$ with
$$J_{\mathrm a}'(E)=\frac{T_{\mathrm{rad}}(E)}{2\pi},\qquad T_{\mathrm{rad}}(E)=\sqrt{2\mu}\int_{r_{-}(E)}^{r_{+}(E)}\frac{\mathrm d\rho}{\sqrt{E-U^{\mathrm{eff}}(\rho)}}\in(0,\infty).$$

3. **(quadrature equals the orbital period)** for a noncircular orbit $0<e<1$ (equivalently $E\in I_0$), the radial coordinate of
   this global extension solves the one-dimensional problem of clause 1 of
   [[pthm-cm05-effective-potential]] with the same energy, and its least
   positive period is the orbital period $T$ of the conic data; the time
   quadrature of that problem is $T_{\mathrm{rad}}(E)=T$, so that
$$J_{\mathrm a}'(E)=\frac{T}{2\pi}=\sqrt{\frac{\mu}{\kappa}}\,a^{3/2},\qquad T^{2}=\frac{4\pi^{2}\mu a^{3}}{\kappa}.$$

4. **(sharpness of the hypotheses)** for $e=0$ the two turning points
   coalesce at the critical point $r_{*}=a$ and the simple-turning-point
   hypothesis of the action-variable theorem fails; the value $J=0$ is
   outside this example (no two-sided bound radial motion), so both
   hypotheses of the construction are genuinely used.

The couplings $\kappa$ and the masses are declared model parameters; no
measured value of $G_{\mathrm N}$ and no empirical premise enters.
items.physical_scope: Assuming countable choice for the orbit suppliers, A worked instance inside the two-label gravitational model of the framework's force branch: on the unique global central-force extension of an elliptic relative orbit ($j=Je_3$, $J>0$, $E<0$, eccentricity $0\le e<1$), the Kepler effective potential has exactly two simple turning points on the energy window between its minimum and $0$; the one-dimensional action variable of the radial problem is $C^1$ there with derivative $T/(2\pi)$; and for a noncircular orbit the radial quadrature is the orbital period, so $J_{\mathrm a}'(E)=T/(2\pi)=\sqrt{\mu/\kappa}\,a^{3/2}$ with $T^2=4\pi^2\mu a^3/\kappa$. The example uses only the model's declared couplings $\kappa=G_{\mathrm N}m_1^{g}m_2^{g}$ and masses; no measured value of $G_{\mathrm N}$ and no empirical premise is used, and no real orbit is claimed to obey the model.

items.title: The zero-energy level of the harmonic model: a compact connected common level set of a completely integrable datum that is a point, not a torus
items.statement:
In a completely integrable datum of a presentation of the framework's force
branch, **every nonempty compact connected common level set of the integral
map is diffeomorphic to a torus $T^{n}=\mathbb R^{n}/\mathbb Z^{n}$.**
items.physical_scope: A counterexample inside the declared harmonic model of the framework's force branch: the one-degree-of-freedom harmonic datum $(H)$ on the generalized-coordinate phase plane of the explicit straight-line immersion is a completely integrable datum, and its zero common level set is compact, connected and nonempty but consists of the single rest point, so it is not diffeomorphic to a torus; equivalently, the level is a critical level at which the regular-fibre hypotheses of the torus theorem fail. The item asserts no measured value and no claim about any apparatus; it shows that regularity cannot be dropped from the hypotheses.

items.title: A free label: a nonempty regular common level set of a completely integrable datum that is noncompact and has no period lattice
items.statement:
In a completely integrable datum of a presentation of the framework's force
branch, **every nonempty regular common level set of the integral map is
compact, and along it the datum's Hamiltonian flow is periodic with a full
lattice of periods.**
items.physical_scope: A counterexample in the autonomous zero-force one-label presentation on R6: the smooth three-integral datum F=(H,p1,p2) on p3>0 has connected regular fibres diffeomorphic to R3, hence noncompact. Its commuting R3 action has trivial stabilizer, so no full period lattice exists, and the physical Hamiltonian flow has no nonzero period. This is declared model data, with no measured value or apparatus claim.

items.title: The conjugate time of the harmonic model: the complete integral's mixed derivative is unbounded and the characteristic family refocuses at $\omega t\in\pi\mathbb Z$
items.statement:
Adopt the harmonic model of [[post-cm04-harmonic-model]] as in the
companion example: one label of mass $m>0$, spring constant $k>0$,
$\omega=\sqrt{k/m}>0$, $T=2\pi/\omega$, branch Hamiltonian
$H(x,p)=p^{2}/(2m)+m\omega^{2}x^{2}/2$, and the family

$$S(t,x,\alpha)=\frac{m\omega}{2}\Bigl[(x^{2}+\alpha^{2})\cot(\omega t)-2x\alpha\,\csc(\omega t)\Bigr]$$
on the open strips where $\sin(\omega t)\neq0$. The example verifies:

1. **(nondegeneracy between conjugate times)** the mixed derivative is
   $$S_{x\alpha}(t)=-\frac{m\omega}{\sin(\omega t)},$$ so $S$ is a complete
   integral of the model's Hamilton-Jacobi equation at every point of
   each time strip $\omega t\in(k\pi,(k+1)\pi)$, and
   $|S_{x\alpha}(t)|\to+\infty$ as $\omega t\to k\pi$ for every
   $k\in\mathbb Z$; the family has a pole there and offers no complete
   integral across it.
2. **(degeneration of the characteristic family)** the characteristic
   curves of $S$ are
$$x(t)=\alpha\cos(\omega t)-\frac{\beta}{m\omega}\sin(\omega t),\qquad\beta=S_{\alpha}(t,x(t),\alpha),$$and the derivative of the position with respect to the Jacobi label
   $\beta$ at fixed $(\alpha,t)$ is
$$\frac{\partial x}{\partial\beta}(t)=-\frac{\sin(\omega t)}{m\omega}=\frac{1}{S_{x\alpha}(t)},$$so it vanishes exactly at the conjugatetimes $\omega t\in\pi\mathbb Z$, where the map from the label $\beta$
   to the position degenerates while $S_{x\alpha}$ is unbounded.
3. **(refocusing of the model's motions)** independently, the harmonic
   motions through a fixed event $(t_{0},x_{0})$, labelled by their
   initial momentum $q$,
$$x(t;q)=x_{0}\cos\bigl(\omega(t-t_{0})\bigr)+\frac{q}{m\omega}\sin\bigl(\omega(t-t_{0})\bigr),$$all satisfy$x(t_{1};q)=-x_{0}$ at the conjugate time
   $t_{1}=t_{0}+\pi/\omega$, for every $q$, and
   $\partial x(t;q)/\partial q=0$ at $t=t_{1}$: the family of model
   solutions through the event refocuses at $(t_{1},-x_{0})$, so no
   label of the family can be recovered from the position there.

All data $m,k$ are declared model parameters and no measured value is
asserted.
items.physical_scope: A worked warning inside the declared harmonic model of the framework's force branch: the explicit complete integral of the oscillator's Hamilton-Jacobi equation is defined only on the time strips between the conjugate times $\omega t\in\pi\mathbb Z$; its mixed derivative $S_{x\alpha}=-m\omega\csc(\omega t)$ is unbounded as those times are approached; and the characteristic family through a fixed event refocuses there (all members with the same initial position pass through the same point a half-period later), so the map from the family's label to the position degenerates. The example asserts no measured value and no claim about any apparatus; it exhibits why the Hamilton-Jacobi statements of this page are local in time and carry no claim across a caustic.
